three-states.title: The staged snapshot is distinct from the editor buffer
three-states.summary: Trace the foundation fixture: committed one, staged two, edited three. A normal commit takes the index; the later working edit remains.

nodes.label: HEAD: one
nodes.description: Previous committed snapshot.

nodes.label: Index: two
nodes.description: git add copied the then-current contents.

nodes.label: Working: three
nodes.description: Later edit has not been staged.

nodes.label: New HEAD: two
nodes.description: Commit snapshots index, not the editor buffer.

steps.title: Inspect the three states
steps.explanation: HEAD, index and working tree each name a different version; none is automatically the other.

steps.title: Read the two diffs
steps.explanation: Cached diff compares HEAD to index. Ordinary diff compares index to working tree. These have different baselines.

steps.title: Commit the index
steps.explanation: The new commit contains two while the working file remains three. The fixture asserts both independently.

history-refs.title: Read parent relationships separately from branch labels
history-refs.summary: The divergent fixture has a common base and a two-parent merge. Branch names move; timestamps do not prove ancestry.

nodes.label: Common base
nodes.description: Shared committed snapshot before divergence.

nodes.label: Main tip
nodes.description: Main adds its policy change.

nodes.label: Feature tip
nodes.description: Feature preserves a different policy change.

nodes.label: Merge commit
nodes.description: Resolved combined snapshot records both parents.

nodes.label: Branch and HEAD references
nodes.description: Names identify current tips; commits retain their parent relationships.

edges.label: main and HEAD resolve to merge

steps.title: Find common ancestry
steps.explanation: Use parent relationships and merge-base rather than dates.

steps.title: Inspect a two-parent merge
steps.explanation: The merge snapshot combines changes; its two parents preserve both lines of history.

steps.title: Distinguish names from objects
steps.explanation: A branch is a movable reference. Useful detached work needs a named reference before leaving it.

conflict-resolution.title: Resolve behavior or deliberately abort the merge
conflict-resolution.summary: The fixture starts clean, aborts its first conflict, then repeats and resolves both illustrative intents. Real combined behavior still needs checks.

nodes.label: Clean starting state
nodes.description: Preserve unrelated edits before beginning integration.

nodes.label: Unresolved merge
nodes.description: Inspect base, ours and theirs in the index.

nodes.label: Deliberate resolution
nodes.description: Choose content that meets the combined requirement.

nodes.label: Stage and complete
nodes.description: Stage the resolved path and create the merge commit.

nodes.label: Review and test
nodes.description: Verify the final combined contents and two-parent result.

nodes.label: Abort recovery
nodes.description: Exit unresolved merge and verify restored main contents.

steps.title: Inspect the three inputs
steps.explanation: Deleting markers alone is not a design decision; read each change and its purpose.

steps.title: Complete a reviewed resolution
steps.explanation: Stage the actual resolution, then inspect and test the combined behavior.

steps.title: Use the explicit abort lifecycle
steps.explanation: The fixture verifies restoration after abort; clean preconditions make recovery more predictable.

remotes-fetch.title: Fetch updates observations before integration changes HEAD
remotes-fetch.summary: The local reviewer clone fetches from the owned source repository. It does not exercise network credentials, branch protection or push.

nodes.label: Source new commit
nodes.description: The fixture source repository advances its main tip.

nodes.label: Reviewer HEAD
nodes.description: Current branch and files remain at the old snapshot.

nodes.label: Fetch objects and refs
nodes.description: Fetch records the source state locally.

nodes.label: Updated origin/main
nodes.description: Remote-tracking reference now includes the descendant.

nodes.label: Review difference
nodes.description: Inspect new commits and choose integration.

nodes.label: Fast-forward HEAD
nodes.description: ff-only advances the reviewer branch if no divergence exists.

steps.title: Record the source separately
steps.explanation: A remote-tracking ref is a local observation of the latest fetched state.

steps.title: Inspect without changing HEAD
steps.explanation: Fetch alone leaves the current branch and working snapshot unchanged.

steps.title: Choose integration deliberately
steps.explanation: ff-only refuses unexpected divergence. Updating refs requires a separate integration choice.

bisect.title: Use one reliable predicate across historical candidates
bisect.summary: Good and bad name the selected behavior. A candidate that cannot test it meaningfully may need skip.

nodes.label: Known good and bad
nodes.description: Bound the search with observed behavior.

nodes.label: Historical candidate
nodes.description: Bisect selects a revision within the range.

nodes.label: Repeatable predicate
nodes.description: Evaluate the same precise regression on the candidate.

nodes.label: Classify observation
nodes.description: Good, bad or skip for unrelated inability to test.

nodes.label: First bad candidate
nodes.description: Search narrows to the regression candidate.

nodes.label: Reproduce and exit
nodes.description: Test candidate and parent, then reset bisect state.

steps.title: Define the behavior
steps.explanation: Pin relevant inputs/dependencies so the predicate means the same thing on each revision.

steps.title: Classify honestly
steps.explanation: A flaky predicate or unrelated build failure can misdirect the search; skip unevaluable candidates.

steps.title: Confirm the boundary
steps.explanation: Reproduce the candidate and its parent before concluding causation; leave bisect mode afterward.

rebase.title: A new base produces new commit identities
rebase.summary: The owned private fixture replays its topic onto main and verifies ancestry and contents. Shared history needs coordination.

nodes.label: Original base
nodes.description: Private topic began at this snapshot.

nodes.label: Old topic commit
nodes.description: Existing commit has the old parent context.

nodes.label: Advanced main
nodes.description: The new agreed base has additional changes.

nodes.label: Replayed topic commit
nodes.description: Reapply selected change after main; identity changes.

nodes.label: Final verification
nodes.description: Inspect new ancestry, dependencies and file contents.

steps.title: Inspect the original history
steps.explanation: A private replay begins from known ownership and base; shared users may depend on old identities.

steps.title: Change the parent context
steps.explanation: Rebase creates a different history, rather than merely changing how the log is displayed.

steps.title: Verify the new candidate
steps.explanation: New parent context needs fresh checks and review. Follow the operation continue/abort lifecycle for conflicts.
